pr_title: Add save clips to Blink services

## Proposed change
<!--

  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

The blinkpy library has been updated to support locally stored video clips.
Blink's local storage mechanism is very slow.  They choose to upload
a clip to their cloud from local storage, and then download it back down.
As a result of this, race conditions make it impossible to get at all the clips
a camera captures.  To mitigate this, new functionality has been added to allow
a user to download all recently-captured videos and download them on a schedule.

https://github.com/fronzbot/blinkpy/commit/47faf5a0ab848805b75e34fd6c996fdfb9f21c9a

issue_context.body:
### The problem

The subject basically says it all. I've been using the Blink integration for a long time with an automation that saves the latest video locally whenever I get a motion detection.

The Blink subscription was the initial free one that has now ended and the automation stopped working.

I have a Sync Module 2 with lots of local storage on a USB stick and can still get at the videos on the local storage through the Blink app (Android) so there must be a way to get at them remotely.

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.11.2

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

2022.11.2

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Supervised

### Integration causing the issue

Blink

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/blink/

I use the new "Save recent clips" service to download all the videos (every 3 minutes) to a local USB drive attached to my HA server. OK - there are some strange things going on with this integration. After my last message (above) around 12:30pm my time, I left the house. I checked again when I got home about 3:30pm and the following had occurred:

I'm glad that is seems to be working (mostly?).

It depends on how often you are calling refresh.

The Blink API returns a manifest containing a list of all your locally-stored videos (on USB).  The `blinkpy` library will call a clip "new" if it's `created_at` timestamp is after the last manifest read.  The manifest read time is only updated if new clips were present.

I would suggest turning on debug logging to try to troubleshoot what is going on.

Here is the relevant function in the library:  https://github.com/fronzbot/blinkpy/blob/87f2746afe016bb20e2fa2cf6032cd8421022d67/blinkpy/sync_module.py#L269

review_comments: I'm confused why you need this function which does the exact same thing as the function above (`_write_video`). I get that you need access to `hass`, but why not just add `hass` as a parameter for this function, move it outside of a function and make it a top level function (not a closure), and then use that in both places?

That is the crux of the PR.  The `_write_video` only triggers a single video (the most recent) to be written.  I left it in so that current users' automations do not break.

The new "save recent clips" adds a service for saving all clips generated since the last refresh.

The documentation PR explains what the new service is doing:
https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/pull/25329/files#diff-c577c832ae063c20a34fc584e3112865f1b8023f3954d149f88b1284a30a6cf3R179
As far as your question about access to `hass`.  I followed the same pattern as the existing `async_handle_save_video_service` function.  I'm not trying to do a refactor here.

The blink integration was calling refresh multiple times.  This uses a `blinkpy` method to check if an update should be called based on the last refresh time.

https://github.com/fronzbot/blinkpy/blob/a40011cb74e6e110cd8a5330e3879e4ac7a50c79/blinkpy/blinkpy.py#L295
